How the weekly comparison works ↓Issue 001 — Current draft ↗
The reading structure

Evidence first.
Then a point of view.

A consistent sequence helps you compare weeks without mistaking a confident story for a proven explanation.

01 / The scorecard

What actually moved?

Checked Friday-to-Friday price returns for the four named benchmarks, with the exact variants, observations and sources recorded.

02 / The evidence

What changed underneath?

Selected economic releases, central bank decisions and company earnings evidence. Facts carry dates and source links.

03 / The mechanism

Why could it matter?

Trace the connection to sales, costs, earnings and valuation. Keep a possible explanation separate from an observed market move.

04 / The countercase

What would change the view?

A plausible alternative, a limitation in the evidence and a condition that would weaken the central interpretation.

05 / The learning desk

One idea to carry forward.

A short explanation and a worked example, connected to the week’s question. Bring your own interpretation to the discussion.

06 / The next questions

What will we check next?

A small, verified watchlist for the following week. Scheduled events are rechecked before release; forecasts remain conditional.

Method / Weekly returns

Compare the same thing,
on the same basis.

For a completed trading week, compare the selected index’s official closing level on the previous Friday with its closing level on the latest completed Friday. For the planned 1 November edition, the intended endpoints are 23 and 30 October 2026.

Weekly price return = (latest Friday close / previous Friday close − 1) × 100

  • Use the same named price-index variant and local currency at both endpoints: USD for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, EUR price variants for the two European benchmarks.
  • Record each observation’s session date, index identifier, source and retrieval time. Check both closing levels before calculating a return.
  • These are price returns. They exclude dividends and currency conversion for an investor whose home currency differs.
  • If Friday is a market holiday, use the latest completed official session on or before that endpoint and label the actual date. Do not silently compare different periods.
  • If an official observation cannot be verified or used with the required permissions, leave the result unavailable and explain the gap. Do not fill it with an ETF proxy or an intraday quote.

The present Wednesday draft has a different purpose: organise the evidence available so far and test the earnings question. Its cutoff is shown on the issue itself.
